newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open flat, pause after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open flat, pause after recent gains.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened steady in thin flows on Wednesday as investors took a break from the recent rally.
"It's going to be a soft day with little volume," said one money market trader with a bank-owned brokerage. "We're due for a little bit of a stall."
Markets rallied ahead of Monday's federal election in which Prime Minister Jean Chretien was re-elected with a slim majority government.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill yield 3.0 percent, flat from the close of trading on Tuesday.
Investors are eying Friday's U.S. unemployment data for indications of whether U.S. inflation is growing at an stronger pace.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill traded to yield 3.34 percent from 3.32 percent. The one-year T-bill traded to yield 3.81 percent from 3.79 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at about 2.95 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
